condition.
Proof.In an uncountable family of determined conditions, thin the finite vertex sets, block-family
supports and tail supports to delta systems. Let𝑠 0 be the vertex root. Thin further so the graph on
𝑠0 agrees throughout. For each shared block-family coordinate, require agreement on membership and
color of every block meeting𝑠0. There are only finitely many such blocks. At each shared tail coordinate
require agreement on membership of each root vertex and its assigned natural color when the coordinate
is a proper coloring. All these comparisons have only countably many patterns.
For any two surviving conditions, use the union of their graphs, with no edge between the two vertex
petals. A block included on only one side at a shared initial coordinate is disjoint from the vertex root.
A pair of blocks newly brought together has no edge between them. The union of the two finite proper
colorings is therefore valid there. At a shared tail coordinate the values agree on root vertices and their
union only introduces comparisons across the petals. Those pairs are nonedges. At a coordinate present
on one side use its original value. Induction through the finite union of the supports verifies that each
assembled prefix strengthens both old prefixes and forces the corresponding constraints. The pair is
compatible. □
